transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

A 'horrible' noise can come from a few different places, so the timing is key. It could be something simple like a coin or button caught in the drain pump filter (usually at the bottom front), an item of clothing rubbing against the drum, or worn suspension parts if it's louder during spin. Could you tell me exactly when the noise happens (e.g. filling, washing, draining, or spinning) and what it sounds like (grinding, rattling, clunking, screeching)?
It's mainly when it spins, a loud roaring rumble like a jet engine. A little noisy on wash but much worse on spin.

A loud roaring rumble that gets much worse during the spin cycle is very characteristic of worn drum bearings. This happens because the inner drum sits on a sealed bearing assembly; once these wear out, they create metal-on-metal friction and play, resulting in that jet-engine noise. To confirm this, please unplug the machine. Open the door and reach inside to grab the inner metal drum (not the rubber seal). Try pushing it in towards the back and pulling it out towards you firmly. Does it feel loose with any 'clunking' play, or does it move stiffly and grind when you turn it by hand? If there is significant play or grinding, the bearings need replacing.
Done it with the power off. There's a clunky up and down play in the drum, and it rumbles/grinds when I turn it by hand.

The 'clunky' up-and-down play combined with the grinding rumble when turning by hand means the internal bearing and spider assembly are worn out or broken. This is a major repair because it involves dismantling the entire machine to check the sealed bearing unit and usually the spider (the metal arm holding the drum). It is not something I can guide you through safely as an owner, as it requires significant disassembly and re-balancing. You will need to call a qualified appliance engineer to carry out this replacement.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Model is ZWF81443W. Is it worth getting it fixed or should I just replace it?

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
Given that model is a Zanussi (part of the Electrolux group), the repair involves replacing both the sealed bearing unit and usually the metal spider arm it sits on, as these often snap together under stress. In most cases, the cost of parts plus an engineer's labour for this major job will be close to or exceed the price of a new machine. Unless you have a specific reason to keep this exact model, I would strongly recommend replacing it rather than repairing it.
